newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Greenpeace stops Rhine ship bringing soya to Swiss.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace stops Rhine ship bringing soya to Swiss.

text.p: Greenpeace activists blocked a grain barge on the Rhine river on Thursday, claiming that it was illegally importing genetically modified soybeans into Switzerland.

The international environment group said about a dozen of its activists had secured the barge Desiree to a jetty in the town of Weil, downriver from the Swiss border at Basel, and chained themselves on board.

A Greenpeace spokesman reached by telephone said his group, along with Swiss consumer and farmer organisations, had filed a complaint with Swiss authorities demanding that the import be stopped and the full cargo confiscated.
Switzerland has not yet decided whether to permit the import and marketing of genetically modified soya and maize. The Federal Health Office is expected to rule on soya this month.
"The food industry does not care at all about the law," Greenpeace said in a statement.
Greenpeace said the ship was bound for the Swiss river port of Kaiseraugst to unload for the Swiss market.
"We know this ship has gene-soya on board because of the grain terminal it loaded from in Rotterdam harbour," the spokesman added.

It was the latest of several Greenpeace blockades in Europe in recent weeks aimed at halting the import of this year's first crop of genetically altered soybeans and soya products from the United States.
The new type of bean was developed by U.S. chemicals group Monsanto to be resistant to its own new "super weedkiller" Roundup.

Environmental groups describe the Roundup technology as a risky experiment with nature while the Monsanto strain has been given a clean bill of health by the U.S. and European Union authorities, who say it poses no danger to the human food chain.
